# Editor's review pack

For Dr Kunda Shahane, editor-in-chief. Everything that needs her decision or signature is in this one document.
Each claim appears once, even if several units use it. Claims she has already verified are not repeated.
Claims that a second AI has not yet confirmed against the source are held back, so that she checks each fact only once.

**4 decision(s). 5 claim(s) to approve again. 424 new claim(s) to check. 14 claim(s) held back until cross-checked.**

## Part A. Decisions

**Q1. ASE guideline, pulsed-wave Doppler of the aortic arch and isthmus. The text (p. 689) includes 'arches' in the minimum assessment; Table 6 (p. 693) marks the transverse arch and isthmus optional and separately requires the distal ductus arteriosus. ChatGPT's check of the PDF confirmed that the guideline does not reconcile the two. How should the course teach it?**

- [ ] Teach as optional (as in Table 6)
- [ ] Teach as required (as in the text)
- [ ] Keep the present wording: state both, teach neither as the rule

If no answer: Present wording stays: units F1 and XA5 state the disagreement and teach neither reading as the rule.
Affects: Units F1 and XA5

**Q2. After a normal early (11 to 14 week) heart check, may unit D9 say plainly that the full second-trimester cardiac screen is still required? The ASE guideline says this for early fetal echocardiography (repeat at 18 to 20 weeks); the ISUOG screening guideline does not say it in so many words.**

- [ ] Yes, say it plainly for screening as the editor's teaching
- [ ] No, keep it as the ASE statement about echocardiography only

If no answer: D9 quotes the ASE statement under its own heading and makes no rule for screening.
Affects: Unit D9

**Q3. Rate thresholds. ISUOG (screening): refer for a persistent rate of 110 or less, or 180 or more. ASE (echocardiography): a sustained rate below 120, or above 160 to 180, is abnormal. Units D8 and F2 teach the ISUOG thresholds for the screener and mention the ASE wording. Is that right for this course?**

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No, teach this instead: ____________

If no answer: As drafted: ISUOG thresholds for the screener, ASE wording mentioned.
Affects: Units D8, D10, F2

**Q4. Does the consent held for archive cases cover publication for teaching in a paid product (not only clinical care)?**

- [ ] Yes, wording covers it
- [ ] No or unsure: re-consent or do not use
- [ ] Ask the legal advisor

If no answer: No archive clip is published until this is confirmed in writing.
Affects: All clip drills and the case atlas

Reworded after the cross-check found: Technical factors, Zoom, cine-loop and image storage, p. 789 also calls for appropriate patient identification in the clinical examination record and consideration of local or national archiving standards. Laterality and orientation labels alone do not cover its documentation instructions. | AH14-309 | Infants with ventricular or atrioventricular septal defect are stable until pulmonary resistance falls, usually weeks after birth; no specialised delivery room care is recommended. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Perinatal Management and Outcome of Fetuses With CHD, CHD With Minimal Risk During Transition, p. 2224 | Z3 | |
| AH14-310 | Ductal-dependent lesions need prostaglandin infusion soon after birth; delivery at a centre with a neonatologist and access to paediatric cardiology is recommended. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Perinatal Management and Outcome of Fetuses With CHD, Ductal-Dependent Lesions, p. 2224 | Z3 | |
| AH14-311 | Ductal-dependent pulmonary circulation is predicted by aorta-to-pulmonary flow in the ductus or reversed ductal orientation (inferior angle below 90°), and ductal-dependent systemic circulation by left-to-right atrial flow; for these, no specialised delivery room care is needed (Class I, LOE B) and prostaglandin E1 is started (I, B). **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225 | Z3 | |
| AH14-312 | In HLHS with restrictive or intact atrial septum, a pulmonary vein forward-to-reverse velocity-time integral ratio below 3, or no change in branch pulmonary artery pulsatility with third-trimester maternal hyperoxygenation, should lead to a plan for possible urgent decompression of the left atrium (Class IIa, LOE B). **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225 | Z3 | |
| AH14-313 | In D-transposition, a small or abnormal ductus with concerns about the foramen ovale indicates high risk of compromise and need for urgent balloon septostomy; such fetuses should be delivered where hypoxia and pulmonary hypertension can be managed. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Perinatal Management and Outcome of Fetuses With CHD, Foramen Ovale-Dependent Lesions, p. 2225 | Z3 | |
| AH14-315 | Planned cardioversion or antiarrhythmic therapy in the delivery room is indicated for uncontrolled tachycardia; planned chronotropic drugs or pacing in the early newborn period is reasonable for complete heart block. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Perinatal Management and Outcome of Fetuses With CHD, Fetal Arrhythmias, p. 2226 | Z3 | |
| AH14-317 | Level of care P: heart disease with palliative care planned (with a severe or fatal chromosomal or multisystem disease); arrange family support and palliative care; normal delivery at the local hospital. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223 | Z3 | |
| AH14-318 | Level of care 1: heart disease without predicted instability in the delivery room or first days (for example VSD, AVSD, mild tetralogy); normal delivery at the local hospital with routine care and later cardiology review. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223 | Z3 | |
| AH14-319 | Level of care 2: minimal risk of instability in the delivery room but needing catheterisation or surgery after birth (ductal-dependent lesions such as HLHS, critical coarctation, severe aortic stenosis, interrupted arch, PA/IVS, severe tetralogy); consider planned induction near term, delivery at a hospital with a neonatologist and accessible cardiology, start prostaglandin if indicated, then transfer. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223 | Z3 | |
| AH14-320 | Level of care 3: likely instability in the delivery room needing immediate specialist stabilisation (d-TGA with concerning atrial septum primum - all d-TGA without an atrial septal defect may reasonably be considered at risk - uncontrolled arrhythmias, complete heart block with heart failure); planned induction at 38-39 weeks, caesarean if needed to coordinate, delivery where rapid stabilising care is possible, neonatologist and cardiac specialist in the delivery room. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223 | Z3 | |
| AH14-321 | Level of care 4: expected instability at placental separation needing immediate catheterisation or surgery in the delivery room (HLHS with severely restrictive or intact atrial septum; d-TGA with severely restrictive or intact atrial septum and abnormal ductus; obstructed TAPVR; Ebstein with hydrops; tetralogy with absent pulmonary valve and severe airway obstruction; uncontrolled arrhythmia with hydrops; complete heart block with low ventricular rate, endocardial fibroelastosis or hydrops); caesarean in a cardiac facility with specialists in the delivery room, usually at 38-39 weeks. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223 | Z3 | |
| AH14-322 | Level of care 5: heart disease for which transplantation is planned (HLHS with intact atrial septum, or heart disease including severe Ebstein or cardiomyopathy with severe ventricular dysfunction); listing after 35 weeks, caesarean when a heart is available, specialised cardiac team in the delivery room. **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 19 (level of care assignment), p. 2223 | Z3 | |
| AH14-323 | For obstructed TAPVR, a decompressing vein below the diaphragm or accelerated flow in it should lead to consideration of ECMO (Class IIb, LOE C). **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225 | Z3 | |
| AH14-324 | For complete heart block, a falling cardiovascular profile score (to below 7), very low ventricular rate, reduced function or endocardial fibroelastosis, or hydrops should lead to consideration of early delivery and of chronotropic drugs or temporary pacing in the delivery room (Class IIa, LOE C). **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225 | Z3 | |
| AH14-325 | In d-TGA, foramen ovale findings reported to predict restriction are: septum primum angle below 30° to the atrial septum, bowing of septum primum more than 50% into the left atrium, loss of normal swinging motion, and a hypermobile septum primum; these call for planned urgent balloon atrial septostomy, on site if possible (Class I, LOE B), and prostaglandin E1 (I, B). **Note:** The table adds that all fetuses with d-TGA and a concerning septum primum should be considered at risk. Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225 | Z3 | |

| AH14-328 | In Ebstein anomaly with hydrops or uncontrolled arrhythmia, early delivery may be considered, with measures to lower pulmonary resistance, treat arrhythmia and support output (Class IIb, LOE C). **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225 | Z3 | |
| AH14-329 | In tachyarrhythmia with rapid rate, reduced function, or pericardial effusion or hydrops, early delivery should be considered if gestation is appropriate, with urgent cardioversion or medical therapy in the delivery room if possible (Class I, LOE C). **Note:** Checked by the extractor (Claude) against the printed page or table on 17 Nov 2026. | AHA-2014-FETALCARDIAC: Table 20 (fetal predictors for delivery planning), p. 2225 | Z3 | |

| AS23-004 | Curvilinear transducers are preferred; linear and sector transducers may also be used. | AS23-008 | The study should include still images, moving clips and a structured report.
